title: Sequence emission atlas: per-step timing + KV cache influence attribution
creator: Ayesha Malik
description:
Goal: build a production-safe token/step-level attribution pipeline that surfaces how much latency and downstream cost each emission (token or step) incurs and how KV cache behavior (hit/miss/warm) shifts those numbers. This ticket covers: 1) lightweight tracing hooks emitted by the serving runtime for every emission step, 2) a sampling and aggregation pipeline to reduce cardinality while preserving tail behavior, 3) a storage & query model for sequence-level heatmaps, and 4) dashboard widgets that highlight cache-influence and device skew.

Why this is different: existing instrumentation captures per-request totals and occasional token probes. We need continuous, queryable attribution without blowing up telemetry cost or adding tail latency. The approach taken here emphasizes delta attribution (per-step delta vs. request baseline), explicit KV cache annotations, and sequence-position-aware aggregation so product and infra teams can reason about where cost/latency concentrates in typical workloads.

Design summary:
- Tracing hooks: emit a minimal span for each emission step: fields = [request_id, model_version, device_id, step_index, token_length, start_ms, end_ms, kv_state]. kv_state is one of {cold_miss, warm_hit, warmed_during_sequence}. Spans must be emitted asynchronously to the metrics emitter to avoid blocking the runtime hot path.
- Sampling: adopt a two-tier sampler: deterministic head-sampling for the first N steps (N=8) on all requests + reservoir sampling of tail steps (p=0.003) with higher retention for requests that hit latency/error SLOs. This keeps heatmaps accurate for heads while still surfacing tail outliers.
- Aggregation & storage: ingest spans into a streaming aggregation job that emits two derived metrics sets: (A) sequence heatmap buckets (model x sequence-length-bucket x step-index-bucket) for visualization, and (B) per-device + per-model 99/95/50 percentile step timings annotated by kv_state. We'll store aggregated rows keyed by day and model so queries for dashboards are cheap.
- Dashboards & alerts: new dashboard panels in Console: "Emission Atlas" showing a stacked heatmap (latency density by step index), "KV Influence" showing % of total latency attributable to KV miss events, and a "Device Skew" panel to find devices with disproportionate tail latency. Add alerting on sustained (>30m) increase in kv-miss-attributed 95th percentile.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Runtime emits step spans with the required fields and does not increase p99 request latency by more than 0.5ms on our benchmark harness.
- Aggregation pipeline produces daily heatmap tiles for at least the last 28 days and exposes a REST endpoint for dashboard queries.
- Console contains two new panels (Emission Atlas, KV Influence) that load within 2s for 28-day queries.
- Alert rule and runbook exist for KV-miss-inflation incidents.

Implementation notes and trade-offs: 
- To avoid cardinality explosion we avoid attaching full prompt text to spans. A request-level prompt-hash can be correlated post-hoc if needed.
- Using reservoir sampling for tails means some individual outliers may be dropped; to mitigate, we force-retain any spans tied to request-level SLO violations.
- Initial rollout will be behind a feature flag with telemetry-rate soft limits so we can ramp without affecting billing.

Telemetry schema and storage pointers (implementation detail notes, not nested):
- span fields: request_id (string), step_index (int), start_ms (int), end_ms (int), elapsed_ms (float), kv_state (string), model (string), device (string), sequence_length (int)
- aggregated tiles: day, model, sequence_length_bucket, step_index_bucket, count, avg_ms, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, kv_miss_fraction

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for 1% of live traffic on staging devices, validate overhead and schema.
- Phase 2 (ramp): 10% -> 50% with alerts enabled; compare heatmaps vs. sampled probe baselines.
- Phase 3 (GA): default enable for hosted, opt-in for Dedicated/Private with config toggles and retention controls.

Runbook and privacy: do not send prompt text; only store prompt-hash when needed. Ensure KMS controls for telemetry export to partners.

Notes for reviewers: focus on sampling parameters, heatmap bucket definitions, and dashboard UI latency budget.
